sections.content: You now have four ways to say what happened to something. Ask two questions. First: do you want to name who did it? Second: are you describing the action or its result? Active verb: the doer is the subject (*El alcalde aprobó el plan*). *Ser* passive: the thing is the subject and the doer is named with *por* (*El plan fue aprobado por el alcalde*). Passive *se* from B1 Unit 6: no doer, general or unknown (*Se aprobó el plan*). *Estar* + participle: the result (*El plan ya está aprobado*).

sections.title: Same event, four choices
rows: The mayor approved the plan. (the doer matters)
El plan fue aprobado por el alcalde.
The plan was approved by the mayor. (the plan first, doer named)
The plan is already approved. (the result)

items.spanish: Se anunciaron los resultados esta mañana.
items.english: The results were announced this morning.

items.spanish: Los resultados fueron anunciados por el jurado.
items.english: The results were announced by the jury.
The results have already been announced.

sections.content: English uses the passive a lot, so English speakers tend to use the *ser* passive too much. In Spanish, if no doer is named, *se* is usually the natural choice, and if the doer is the point, an active verb is. Do not use *se* together with *por* and a doer: *Se aprobó el plan por el alcalde* is wrong.
